title: European Commons
purpose: Recover the conversation-developed idea of a European cultural/public digital commons connecting media, creators, communities, rights and portability. This is a project proposal, not a claim that such a unified platform currently exists.
core_thesis: Culture should be treated as infrastructure: identities, creative works, audiences, rights and communities should be portable and interoperable rather than trapped in isolated platforms.

platform_principles.open_apis: Core public interfaces should allow compatible third-party clients, tools and services.
platform_principles.user_portability: People should be able to export and move their identity, subscriptions, social graph and content metadata where lawful.
platform_principles.creator_ownership: Creators retain clear rights and portable records around their works, audiences and monetization relationships.
platform_principles.competing_algorithms: Users should be able to choose among ranking/recommendation systems instead of being locked into one compulsory algorithmic feed.
platform_principles.public_domain: Public-domain works should be easy to discover, reuse and contextualize.
platform_principles.interoperability: Shared protocols should reduce platform lock-in without requiring one centralized operator to control all activity.

rights_layer.machine_readable_rights: Represent relevant licenses, territories, durations, attribution requirements and reuse permissions in standardized machine-readable form.
rights_layer.european_rights_exchange: A proposed interoperable discovery/clearing layer for rights metadata and lawful licensing transactions, not a single monopoly owner of culture.
rights_layer.cultural_pass: A portable identity/entitlement layer for access to participating cultural institutions, archives, events or public-interest media services.
rights_layer.auditability: Rights decisions and takedowns should expose reasons, provenance and appeal paths where legally possible.

institutional_model.commons_not_monolith: The intended architecture is federated/interoperable rather than one centralized super-platform.
institutional_model.public_private_mix: Public institutions, broadcasters, archives, independent creators and private services can participate under compatible standards.
institutional_model.locality: Language, regional identity and national cultural institutions remain visible rather than being flattened into one generic European feed.

economic_link: The Commons connects to the European Coupling Programme because culture also has rights, contracts, payments, identity, provenance and cross-border friction. Cultural interoperability is an economic as well as civic capability.
epistemic_link: News and documentary layers should expose sources, corrections and provenance rather than treating virality as evidence.
success_test: Does the system increase cultural access, creator agency, portability and pluralism without recreating a single compulsory gatekeeper?
